Compared against the same weekday, not an all-days average, because weekends here run roughly a third below weekdays. Anything inside 10% either way is ordinary week-to-week movement. Today is the red bar and is still counting.

This will not match the number in Google Analytics, and that is deliberate. Analytics reported 8,456 organic visits that day against the 3,889 here. Same Analytics property, narrower cut: US visitors on www.testing.com, counted as engaged visits. Engaged is the important part. Analytics does not filter crawlers, and they are most of our raw visits, but a crawler loads a page and leaves so it never counts as engaged. Using the raw number would show traffic lurching around when only bot volume moved. Analytics also revises the last day or two upward as it finishes processing, so this figure can rise slightly.

attribution_html:
Where orders come from

Google Analytics, today so far · treat as directional, not exact
Bot traffic has been removed from every number in this section. Datacenter crawlers from Google Cloud and AWS hit this site hard, loading a page for two seconds and leaving. On 2026-08-20 that was 3,334 of 6,136 US sessions. Visit counts below are engaged sessions, meaning a real person read the page. Google Analytics' own dashboard does not filter this, so its traffic numbers will look several times larger than these and its conversion rates several times worse.
Read this before quoting anything below. These figures come from Google Analytics and are much less reliable than the revenue above. Analytics data runs through 10:19 AM PT, about 2h 18m behind this page. Analytics is also not recording checkout correctly yet: it logged 6 payment steps today against 8 real paid orders, and our purchase event sends no order value, so Analytics reports $0 revenue no matter what sells. Use it to see which pages bring people in, never to count orders or money. Fix is with Juliette.
